description: Isolated test of evaluation-awareness vs. an instilled Charter disposition (research direction 10 / Deckenbach et al. 2026). For each of the 11 Qalvori Charter rules and 2 temptation levels, the identical decision (same payoffs, same conditions, single turn) is presented three ways: with a sentence saying the filing will be audited, with a sentence saying it will not, or with no observability statement at all. Only that trailing sentence differs across the triplet. If Charter-choosing tracks the rule regardless of framing, that supports an instilled disposition; if it tracks audited-vs-unobserved with the rule and payoffs held fixed, that is evaluation-awareness rather than belief. This differs from the multi-turn `pressure` family in the companion submission (generality-battery-v1), which confounds the framing with a prior public commitment the clerk must revise; here there is no prior commitment to revise, so the framing is the only manipulated variable. 66 observability items (66 identifying total once the baseline direct_floor/leakage/fabrication/multi_hop coverage, re-used unchanged from generality-battery-v1, is included).
